page: Amazon Web Services c6i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an x86_64 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processor (model 8375C) running at a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. Hardware allocation includes 16 vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI, as well as hardware cryptographic features like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory provisioning stands at 32.0 GB of DDR4 system RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). In memory benchmarks, the system produces 828.26 GB/sec for small-block cached reads, 95.59 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads, and 55.33 GB/sec for sequential writes. The instance does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. No discrete GPU accelerators are present on this platform.

Across compute benchmarks, the instance yields average tier results relative to peer hardware, posting a Geekbench single-core score of 1604.0, a multi-core score of 9680.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 21033.65. Application benchmarks record 15.63 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 22.41 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and single-threaded gzip compression of 27.9 GB/sec. Software compilation using Clang achieves a Geekbench sub-score of 15145.0. However, medium-scale machine learning tasks exhibit constraints, with 7B parameter LLM prompt processing registering in the bottom quartile at 31.59 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware acceleration.

The c6i.4xlarge delivers balanced compute density and CPU-intensive cost efficiency where moderate memory is sufficient. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage and limited memory depth relative to core count. The instance is appropriate for batch computing, CI/CD build farms, web server fleets, application backend services, and intermediate distributed data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c6i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without discrete GPU acceleration or bundled local storage. External networking provides a baseline throughput of 6 Gbps. Standard benchmarks position the system in the average performance tier, achieving 15472.98 in stress-ng multi-core, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9680.0, and 15.63 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware instruction support spans AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI. The instance offers resource efficiency for compute-focused workloads that do not demand large per-core memory footprints, making it well matched for Clang compilation pipelines, CI/CD runners, distributed microservices, web serving infrastructure, and CPU-based computational tasks.
